examples.en: I turn into a sleepyhead every weekend.
My older brother is a well-known late riser.
It's hard waking up my sleepyhead son.

examples.ko: 주말이면 늦잠꾸러기 친구가 열 시까지 자요.
examples.en: On weekends my sleepyhead friend sleeps until ten.

examples.ko: 어릴 때는 늦잠꾸러기라서 학교에 자주 늦었어요.
examples.en: As a kid I was a late sleeper, so I was often late for school.

examples.ko: 늦잠꾸러기도 아침 운동을 하면 달라질 수 있어요.
examples.en: Even a sleepyhead can change by exercising in the morning.

explain: 늦잠을 자는 사람을 귀엽게 놀릴 때 써요. 가족이나 친구 사이에서 장난스럽게 쓰고, 어른에게는 쓰지 않아요. '-꾸러기'는 어떤 특징이 강한 사람에게 붙는 말이에요.

phrases.en: I sleep in on Sundays.
phrases.nuance_ko: '늦잠꾸러기'의 바탕이 되는 말이에요. 누구에게나 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: The base expression of 늦잠꾸러기; fine to use about anyone.

phrases.en: My son loves sleeping.
phrases.nuance_ko: 잠이 많은 사람을 귀엽게 말하는 비슷한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A similar word for someone who sleeps a lot, said fondly.

phrases.en: Waking up my sleepyhead sibling is quite a job.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가족이나 친구를 장난스럽게 부를 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used playfully for a family member or friend.

explain_en: It teases someone who oversleeps in a cute way. It is used playfully among family and friends, but not to elders. The ending '-꾸러기' attaches to a person with a strong trait.

examples.en: You have to watch what you say at work.
Please be careful with your words in front of elders.
Even though I was angry, I should have watched my words.
He is being careful with his words in front of reporters.
If you don't watch your words, misunderstandings happen.
Many people watch their words on social media too.

explain: '말조심하세요'는 친절한 충고도 되지만, 짧은 '말조심해!'는 화가 난 경고로 들릴 수 있어요. 친구에게 부드럽게 말할 때는 '조심해서 말해 줘'가 편해요.

phrases.en: Please watch what you say here.
phrases.nuance_ko: 존댓말로 하는 충고예요. 친절하게 들리게 말하면 좋아요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite piece of advice; it sounds kind with a gentle tone.

phrases.en: I speak carefully to my friend.
phrases.nuance_ko: '말조심하다'보다 부드럽고 편하게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A softer, more casual alternative to '말조심하다'.

phrases.en: He doesn't watch his words, so he often fights.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조심 없이 말하는 사람을 말할 때 부정형으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form describes someone who speaks carelessly.

explain_en: 말조심하세요 can be friendly advice, but the short 말조심해! can sound like an angry warning. To a friend, a softer way is 조심해서 말해 줘.

en: annoying-looking person; someone who looks unlikable

examples.ko: 그 친구는 말투 때문에 밉상으로 보여요.
examples.en: That friend comes across as annoying because of the way they talk.
Even someone annoying grows on you the more you see them.

examples.ko: 회사에 밉상 동료가 한 명 있어요.
examples.en: There's one annoying coworker at my company.
You only pick the things that make people dislike you.

examples.ko: 저는 괜히 밉상이 된 것 같아요.
examples.en: I feel like I've become disliked for no reason.
My younger sibling is being really annoying today.

explain: 생김새보다는 하는 행동이나 말투 때문에 얄밉고 정이 안 가는 사람이라는 느낌으로 많이 써요. '밉상 짓', '밉상 동료'처럼 말해요. 반대 느낌의 말은 '귀염상'이나 '호감형'이에요.

phrases.example: 그 친구는 밉상 짓을 자꾸 해요.
phrases.en: That friend keeps doing annoying things.
phrases.nuance_ko: 얄밉고 정이 안 가는 행동을 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to behavior that is irritating and off-putting.

phrases.example: 밉상 동료 때문에 회사 가기가 힘들어요.
phrases.en: Because of an annoying coworker, going to work is hard.
phrases.nuance_ko: 함께 일하는 사람이 얄미울 때 쓰는 구어체 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A casual phrase for a coworker who is irritating.

phrases.en: If you lie, people will dislike you.
phrases.nuance_ko: 행동 때문에 사람들이 싫어하게 되는 상황에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone becomes disliked because of their behavior.

explain_en: It is used more for someone who is annoying or hard to like because of their behavior or way of talking than because of their looks. You hear it in phrases like '밉상 짓' and '밉상 동료'. Words with the opposite feel are '귀염상' and '호감형'.

examples.en: He was called a traitor by his friends.
The traitor in the movie was revealed at the end.

examples.ko: 저는 배신자라는 말을 듣고 많이 속상했어요.
examples.en: I was very upset to be called a traitor.

examples.ko: 그는 회사의 비밀을 알려 준 배신자예요.
examples.en: He is the traitor who gave away the company's secrets.
It is not easy to forgive a betrayer.

examples.ko: 아무도 배신자와 같이 일하고 싶어 하지 않아요.
examples.en: Nobody wants to work with a traitor.

explain: 믿던 사람을 속이거나 등진 사람을 가리킬 때 써요. 친구나 동료에게 쓰면 아주 강한 비난이라서 조심해야 해요. '변절자'는 주로 생각이나 편을 바꾼 사람에게 써요.

phrases.en: My friend betrayed me.
phrases.nuance_ko: '배신자'의 동사 형태로, 믿음을 깨는 행동을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb form of 배신자; describes the act of breaking trust.

phrases.en: Everyone treated him like a traitor.
phrases.nuance_ko: 실제로 배신했는지와 상관없이 그렇게 대한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means treating someone as a traitor, whether or not they were.

phrases.en: I don't want to become a traitor.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자신이 그런 사람이 되는 것을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to talk about becoming that kind of person.

explain_en: It refers to a person who deceived or turned against someone who trusted them. Calling a friend or colleague this is a very strong accusation, so be careful. '변절자' is mainly for someone who switched beliefs or sides.

examples.en: My mom is a notorious nagger.
My ears hurt because of my nagging older sister.
That teacher is a nagger, so students avoid her.
I don't want to become a nagger.
My husband teases me by calling me a nag.

examples.ko: 잔소리꾼도 다 나를 생각해서 그러는 거죠.
examples.en: Even naggers do it because they care about me.

explain: 가족이나 친한 사이에서 농담 반으로 많이 써요. 면전에서 말하면 기분 나쁘게 들릴 수 있어요. '장사꾼', '일꾼'처럼 '-꾼'이 붙은 말과 같이 기억하면 좋아요.

phrases.en: My sister seems like a nagger today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 누군가가 평소보다 잔소리가 많을 때 가볍게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A light remark when someone is nagging more than usual.

phrases.en: The older he gets, the more of a nagger my dad becomes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 변해서 잔소리가 많아졌다는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Suggests someone has changed and nags more now.

phrases.en: Mom nags me to go to bed early.
phrases.nuance_ko: '잔소리꾼'은 사람이고, '잔소리를 하다'는 그 행동을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: '잔소리꾼' is the person; '잔소리를 하다' is the action.

explain_en: It is often used half jokingly among family or close friends. Saying it to someone's face can offend them. It helps to learn it with other '-꾼' words such as '장사꾼' and '일꾼'.

en: to sever ties; to break off a friendship

examples.en: I had a big fight with that friend and we cut ties.
If I break off with a friend, I feel very uncomfortable.

examples.ko: 우리 절교하자는 말은 절대 하지 마요.
examples.en: Never say that we should stop being friends.
Why did you end up cutting ties with that person?

examples.ko: 형은 오랜 친구와 절교한 뒤 많이 외로워했어요.
examples.en: My brother felt very lonely after ending his long friendship.
Are you sure you won't regret it even if you cut ties?

explain: '~와/과 절교하다'처럼 '와/과'나 '랑'과 함께 써요. 연인 사이에는 '헤어지다'가 자연스럽고, '절교하다'는 친구나 지인 사이에 써요.

phrases.en: I cut ties with my friend yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 관계를 끊었다는 과거 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Past tense: the friendship has already ended.

phrases.en: They keep lying, so I want to end the friendship.
phrases.nuance_ko: 마음을 말할 때 '-고 싶다'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adds -고 싶다 to express a wish.

phrases.en: Please don't end your friendship over a small thing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말리는 말로 쓰는 부정 명령형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A negative command used to urge someone not to.

explain_en: It is used as '~와/과 절교하다' or with '랑'. For couples '헤어지다' is natural; '절교하다' is for friends and acquaintances.

en: to be loyal; to be devoted

examples.en: He stayed loyal to one company all his life.
The retainers had to be loyal to the king.
There are many soldiers devoted to their country.
What do you get from being loyal to the boss?

examples.ko: 팀에 충성하고 싶어서 다른 제안을 거절했어요.
examples.en: I wanted to stay loyal to my team, so I turned down other offers.
I will be loyal to the work rather than the company.

explain: '왕에게', '나라에'처럼 조사 '에게/에'와 같이 써요. 목적어를 바로 받지 않아서 '왕을 충성하다'는 틀려요. 비슷한 '헌신하다'는 자기 시간과 힘을 내놓는 느낌이 더 강해요.

phrases.en: Soldiers must be loyal to their country.
phrases.nuance_ko: '에' 조사를 붙여 충성하는 대상을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The particle 에 marks the one you are loyal to.
phrases.en_equiv: to be loyal to the country

phrases.en: That official stayed loyal to the king to the end.
phrases.nuance_ko: '끝까지'를 붙여 변하지 않는 마음을 강조해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 끝까지 stresses an unchanging devotion.
phrases.en_equiv: to stay loyal to the end

phrases.en: There aren't many people loyal to the company.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동사를 명사 앞에 붙이는 활용형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb in modifier form placed before a noun.

explain_en: Use it with the particle 에게 or 에, as in '왕에게' or '나라에'. It does not take a direct object, so '왕을 충성하다' is wrong. The similar 헌신하다 feels more like giving up your own time and energy.

t90.ax: The retainers had to be loyal to the king.

examples.en: It's a story about a person who became corrupt chasing money.
He went astray after he became successful.

examples.ko: 아이들이 타락하지 않게 부모가 잘 가르쳐야 해요.
examples.en: Parents must teach well so their children don't go astray.

examples.ko: 사람은 쉽게 타락할 수 있다는 걸 이 소설이 보여 줘요.
examples.en: This novel shows that people can easily become corrupt.

examples.ko: 큰 힘을 가지면 타락하기 쉽다는 말이 있어요.
examples.en: There's a saying that it's easy to become corrupt when you hold great power.
It hurt me that my friend had gone astray.

explain: 사람의 마음이나 생활이 나쁜 쪽으로 무너질 때 써요. 강한 말이라 사람에게 직접 쓰면 무례해요. 작은 실수는 '잘못하다'라고 해요.

phrases.example: 그는 타락한 생활을 끝내고 새로 시작했어요.
phrases.en: He ended his depraved life and started anew.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸며 주는 활용형이에요. 이야기나 글에서 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The form that modifies a noun, used often in stories and writing.

phrases.en: He did not go astray even in hard times.
phrases.nuance_ko: '타락하다'의 부정형으로, 마음이나 태도를 지켰다는 칭찬의 뜻이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, carrying a sense of praise for keeping one's heart and attitude.

phrases.example: 돈이 많아지면서 그는 점점 타락해 갔어요.
phrases.en: As he got more money, he gradually went bad.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조금씩 나빠지는 과정을 보여 줘요. 변화의 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Shows a gradual process of getting worse, with a sense of change.

explain_en: Used when a person's character or lifestyle falls apart in a bad direction. It is a harsh word, so saying it directly to someone is rude. For small mistakes, use '잘못하다'.

examples.en: The brothers bicker from the morning.

examples.ko: 두 사람은 만나면 티격태격하지만 사이가 좋아요.
examples.en: Those two squabble whenever they meet, but they get along well.
The kids bickered over the order of the game.
The couple always go around together even while bickering.
I heard the sounds of squabbling from the next room.

examples.ko: 드라마 속 두 주인공은 티격태격하다가 사랑에 빠져요.
examples.en: The two leads in the drama bicker and then fall in love.

explain: 크게 싸우는 게 아니라 사소한 일로 자꾸 다투는 모습이에요. 가까운 사이라서 가볍게 다툰다는 정다운 느낌이 있어요. '싸우다'보다 약하고 '다투다'보다 더 가볍게 쓰는 말이에요.

phrases.en: They squabble but still go everywhere together.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다투지만 사이가 좋다는 것을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used to say they quarrel yet get along well.

phrases.en: The siblings bicker with each other.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부사 '티격태격'을 동사 앞에 붙인 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adverb placed before a verb.

phrases.en: The two argued back and forth over money.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서로 자기 말이 맞다고 다투는 모습으로, 뜻이 비슷해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar meaning: arguing back and forth over who is right.

explain_en: It shows two people repeatedly arguing over small things, not fighting hard. It has a warm tone because they are usually close. It is weaker than 싸우다 and lighter than 다투다.

examples.en: It has been drizzling since morning, so the road is damp.

examples.ko: 이 정도 가랑비는 우산 없이 맞아도 괜찮아요.
examples.en: This much drizzle is fine to walk in without an umbrella.

examples.ko: 가랑비 오는 날에는 파전이 먹고 싶어요.
examples.en: On drizzly days I want to eat scallion pancakes.

examples.ko: 산책하는 동안 가랑비를 맞았더니 머리가 젖었어요.
examples.en: I got caught in the drizzle during my walk and my hair got wet.
I worried the sports day would be postponed because of the drizzle.
Outside the window, a fine rain like a drizzle is falling.

explain: 가늘게 조용히 내리는 비를 말해요. 이슬비, 보슬비도 비슷하게 가늘게 내리는 비이고, 반대 느낌은 갑자기 세게 쏟아지는 '소나기'예요. 속담에 자주 나와요.

phrases.example: 작은 지출도 쌓이면 커져요. 가랑비에 옷 젖는 줄 모른다더니 카드값이 많이 나왔어요.
phrases.en: Small expenses pile up. As the saying goes, you don't notice a drizzle soaking your clothes, and my card bill came out high.
phrases.nuance_ko: 작고 사소한 것이라도 쌓이면 큰 영향을 준다는 속담이에요. 돈, 습관, 나쁜 버릇 이야기에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A proverb meaning that even small things have a big effect when they accumulate. Often used for money, habits and bad habits.
phrases.en_equiv: Many a little makes a mickle

explain_en: Thin, light rain, a bit thicker than mist; general term (가랑비에 옷 젖는 줄 모른다) It is a thin, quiet rain. '이슬비' and '보슬비' are also fine, light rains, while the opposite feel is '소나기', a sudden heavy shower. It appears in a well-known proverb.

t90.ax: On drizzly days I want to eat scallion pancakes.

examples.en: Buds have started to form on the cherry tree.

examples.ko: 며칠 지나면 꽃봉오리가 활짝 필 거예요.
examples.en: In a few days the buds will bloom fully.
It's still a bud, so it's fine to put it in a vase.
I carefully touched the rose bud.

examples.ko: 봄비가 내린 뒤 꽃봉오리가 통통하게 부풀었어요.
examples.en: After the spring rain, the buds swelled up plump.
One flower bud burst open this morning.

explain: 활짝 핀 꽃은 '만개한 꽃', 아직 닫힌 상태는 '꽃봉오리'라고 구별해요. '봉오리'로 줄여 말하기도 하고, 앞날이 기대되는 어린 사람을 '꽃봉오리'에 비유하기도 해요.

phrases.en: A rosebud has come up in the flower bed.
phrases.nuance_ko: '꽃봉오리'를 줄인 말로, 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A shortened form of '꽃봉오리' that is common in speech.

phrases.en: The weather was warm, so the flower buds opened.
phrases.nuance_ko: 닫혀 있던 꽃봉오리가 피기 시작할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for when a closed bud starts to open.

phrases.en: When spring came, flower buds formed on the branches.
phrases.nuance_ko: 꽃봉오리가 처음 생길 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for when buds first form.

explain_en: General word for an unopened flower; also figurative for promising youth. A fully open flower is 만개한 꽃, while one still closed is a 꽃봉오리. It is also shortened to '봉오리', and a promising young person is sometimes compared to a 꽃봉오리.

t90.ax: I carefully touched the rose bud.

examples.en: At night, moths gathered near the light.
A moth came in through the window.

examples.ko: 나방은 나비보다 색이 어두운 경우가 많아요.
examples.en: Moths are often darker in color than butterflies.
I was startled when a moth came out of the closet.
The moth caterpillars ate all the leaves.
I'm scared of moths, so I avoid them.

explain: 나비는 낮에 날고 앉을 때 날개를 접는 경우가 많고, 나방은 밤에 날고 앉을 때 날개를 펴는 경우가 많아요. 밤에 불빛에 모이는 모습 때문에 '불나방'이라는 말도 있는데, 위험한 줄 모르고 뛰어드는 사람을 비유할 때 써요.

phrases.en: Don't jump into dangerous things like a moth to a flame.
phrases.nuance_ko: 불빛에 모이는 나방에서 나온 말로, 위험한 줄 모르는 사람을 비유해요.
phrases.nuance_en: From moths drawn to light; compares someone who rushes into danger without knowing it.

phrases.en: Many moths fly around on summer nights.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나방이 날아다니는 모습을 말할 때 쓰는 문장이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A sentence for describing moths flying around.

phrases.en: Butterflies and moths look alike.
phrases.nuance_ko: 두 곤충을 비교하거나 함께 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when comparing the two insects or mentioning them together.

explain_en: Butterflies tend to fly by day and fold their wings when they rest, while moths tend to fly at night and keep their wings spread when they rest. Because moths gather around lights at night, there is also the word '불나방', used figuratively for someone who rushes into danger without realizing it.

en: to be gently warm; to be softly warm (sunlight)

examples.en: The spring sunshine is warm, so I feel sleepy.
Grandmother's hands were always warm.

examples.ko: 따스한 차 한 잔을 마시니까 마음이 편해졌어요.
examples.en: Drinking a cup of warm tea made me feel at ease.

examples.ko: 그 사람의 따스한 말 한마디에 힘이 났어요.
examples.en: A single warm word from him gave me strength.
When the weather gets warm, let's go on a picnic together.

examples.ko: 따스하게 안아 주는 친구 덕분에 위로가 됐어요.
examples.en: A friend who hugged me warmly comforted me.

explain: '따뜻하다'와 거의 같지만 따스하다는 더 부드럽고 글이나 노래에서 자주 나와요. 햇살, 손, 말, 마음처럼 포근한 것에 잘 어울려요. 뜨거운 국이나 방바닥에는 '따뜻하다'나 '뜨겁다'를 쓰는 편이 자연스러워요.

phrases.example: 따스한 말 한마디가 큰 힘이 돼요.
phrases.en: A warm word can be a great help.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람의 말이나 마음이 포근할 때 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone's words or heart feel gentle and comforting.

phrases.example: 할머니가 따스하게 웃으며 저를 안아 주셨어요.
phrases.en: My grandmother hugged me with a warm smile.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-게'를 붙이면 웃는 모습이나 대하는 방식을 부드럽게 꾸며 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding -게 describes how someone smiles or treats others, in a soft way.

phrases.en: The winter wind is not warm.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로 포근하지 않다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, saying something is not gently warm.

explain_en: It is nearly the same as 따뜻하다, but 따스하다 is softer and appears more in writing and songs. It suits cozy things like sunlight, hands, words, and hearts. For hot soup or a heated floor, 따뜻하다 or 뜨겁다 sounds more natural.

examples.en: White fluffy clouds are floating in the sky.
Fluffy clouds remind me of cotton candy.
The shape of puffy clouds keeps changing.
Sunlight shone through the puffy clouds.
It's a cake as fluffy as a cloud.
I want to lie down on the fluffy clouds.

explain: 몽실몽실하게 위로 솟은 하얀 구름이에요. 맑은 날 여름 하늘에서 많이 보여서 그림이나 동요, 시에 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: The white puffy clouds in the blue sky are pretty.
phrases.nuance_ko: 구름 색을 앞에 붙여서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used with a color word before it.

phrases.en: Puffy clouds rose up in the summer sky.
phrases.nuance_ko: 구름이 위로 솟아오르는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes clouds billowing upward.

phrases.en: Puffy clouds are floating above the mountain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 구름이 하늘에 있는 상태를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the state of clouds being in the sky.

explain_en: These are white clouds that billow upward in rounded puffs. They are often seen in clear summer skies and appear in drawings, children's songs and poems.

examples.en: I keep a small cactus on my desk.

examples.ko: 선인장은 물을 자주 안 줘도 돼요.
examples.en: A cactus doesn't need to be watered often.
I pricked my finger on a cactus spine.
Big cacti grow in great numbers in the desert.
A yellow flower bloomed on the cactus!

examples.ko: 바쁜 사람에게는 선인장 같은 식물을 추천해요.
examples.en: For busy people, I recommend plants like a cactus.

explain: '선인장'은 줄기에 물을 저장해서 물을 적게 줘도 사는 식물이에요. 잎이나 줄기에 물을 저장하는 식물 전체는 '다육식물'이라고 하고, 선인장은 그중 한 종류예요. '가시'와 함께 자주 말해요.

phrases.en: I got pricked by a cactus thorn.
phrases.nuance_ko: 선인장과 가장 자주 같이 말하는 부분이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The part most often mentioned together with cactus.

phrases.en: I grow a cactus on my balcony.
phrases.nuance_ko: 식물을 기를 때는 '키우다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 키우다 for growing a plant.

phrases.example: 선인장에는 한 달에 한 번 물을 줘요.
phrases.en: I water the cactus once a month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 식물에 물을 줄 때는 '에 물을 주다'라고 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: To water a plant, say 에 물을 주다.

explain_en: A 선인장 is a plant that stores water in its stem and survives on very little. The broader group of plants that store water in leaves or stems is 다육식물, and 선인장 is one kind of them. It is often mentioned together with 가시 (thorns).
